root_cause.text: The command stream parsing loop in `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()` increments the buffer index variable without re-validating it against the buffer bounds before writing the second word of a 64-bit command, allowing an out-of-bounds heap write when a 64-bit command (bit 14 set) is encountered at the last valid index.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds a bounds check `if (i >= size / 4) return -EINVAL;` immediately after incrementing the index `i++` and before the second write `bocmds[i] = cmds[1]`. The vulnerability occurs because when `i == size/4 - 1` at loop entry with bit 14 set in the command word, the first write to `bocmds[i]` is valid, but after `i++` increments to `size/4`, the second write `bocmds[i] = cmds[1]` writes four bytes past the end of the DMA-allocated buffer (which has valid indices [0, size/4-1]). The missing bounds check before this second write is the precise root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable construct is present in the `ethosu_gem_cmdstream_copy_and_validate()` function. The loop iterates with `for (i = 0; i < size / 4; i++)` and processes 32-bit command words. When a 64-bit command is detected (bit 14 set: `if (cmd & 0x4000)`), the code reads a second word with `get_user(cmds[1], ucmds++)` and increments the loop index with `i++` and `bocmds[i] = cmds[1]`. However, there is no bounds check on the incremented index `i` before writing `bocmds[i]`. If a 64-bit command appears at the last valid index (i == size/4 - 1), the increment makes i == size/4, which is out of bounds for the bocmds array. The subsequent write `bocmds[i] = cmds[1]` at line with the second word assignment performs an out-of-bounds heap write. The vulnerability exists because the index is incremented without re-validating it against the buffer bounds (size/4) before the write operation.
